about.title: San Bruno Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: San Bruno sees a steady stream of traffic moving between I-280, I-380, and El Camino Real, with Skyline Boulevard adding another layer of commuter and cut-through traffic. Recent public-record data shows 135 injury collisions and 174 people hurt in a single year here, with a noticeable spike on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. as commuters head home. Whether you were rear-ended near the I-380 interchange or sideswiped merging onto El Camino Real, the aftermath can mean medical bills, missed work, and calls from an insurance adjuster before you've even seen a doctor twice. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect injured San Bruno residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate the crash, deal with insurers, and explain your options under California law. There's no fee unless the attorney recovers something for you, and the first conversation costs nothing.
commonInjuries: Soft tissue damage and deep bruising

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Settling

items.title: California's Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: You generally have two years to file a car accident claim, but if a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. An attorney can spot that issue early so you don't lose your claim to a deadline.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Cut Your Recovery
items.desc: California allows you to recover damages even if you're partly at fault, but your share of fault reduces what you can collect. An attorney can push back on an insurer trying to inflate your percentage of blame.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Be Used Against You
items.desc: The other driver's insurer may ask for a recorded statement soon after the crash, hoping you'll say something that limits their payout. An attorney can speak for you and make sure early evidence — dashcam footage, skid marks, witness contacts — isn't lost.

items.question: I was hit near the I-380/El Camino Real interchange — does it matter where the crash happened?
items.answer: It can. Location affects which police jurisdiction responded, where the collision report is filed, and sometimes whether a public roadway design issue is involved. An attorney can pull the right records and figure out who may share responsibility.

items.question: How long do I actually have to file a claim in California?
items.answer: The general rule is two years from the date of the crash, but claims against a government entity — like certain roads or vehicles — can require a claim within six months. Missing either deadline can end your case, so it's worth checking early rather than waiting.

items.question: Should I give the other driver's insurance company a statement?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers sometimes use those statements to argue you were more at fault than you actually were. A free consultation can help you understand what to say and what to hold off on.
